definitions.explanation: The flow of blood from a wound or internal injury. Also used figuratively to mean a significant financial loss.

examples.japanese: {傷口|きずぐち}から{出血|しゅっけつ}している。
{出血|しゅっけつ}が{止|と}まらないので{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: The bleeding wouldn't stop, so I went to the hospital.

examples.japanese: {大量|たいりょう}{出血|しゅっけつ}で{命|いのち}が{危|あぶ}ない{状態|じょうたい}だったが、{手術|しゅじゅつ}で{助|たす}かった。
examples.english: The patient's life was in danger due to massive hemorrhaging, but surgery saved them.

notes:
Compound of {出|しゅつ} (to come out) + {血|けつ} (blood). Primarily a medical term but commonly used in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出血|しゅっけつ}する (to bleed)
- {出血|しゅっけつ}が{止|と}まる (the bleeding stops)
- {出血|しゅっけつ}を{止|と}める (to stop the bleeding)
- {大量|たいりょう}{出血|しゅっけつ} (massive bleeding)
- {内|ない}{出血|しゅっけつ} (internal bleeding)
- {出血|しゅっけつ}{多量|たりょう} (excessive blood loss)
- {出血|しゅっけつ}サービス (selling at a huge loss — figurative)

USAGE:
The figurative expression {出血|しゅっけつ}サービス or {出血|しゅっけつ}{大|おお}サービス means selling at a drastic loss, used in advertising and business contexts to emphasize extreme discounts.

cross_references.notes: 出欠 means attendance/absence — same reading, different meaning
